Distinct-value count in fixed memory

Source: R/skch.R
dstnskch.Rd

HyperLogLog: estimates how many distinct values a column holds using a fixed register per bucket, regardless of the column's length or cardinality. dstnskch() builds or extends the registers, dstncnt() turns them into an estimate, and skchmrg() combines two sketches.

Usage

dstnskch(x, p = 14L, regstr = NULL)

dstncnt(regstr)

skchmrg(a, b)

Arguments

x

A vector, compared as text.

p

Log2 of the register count, a whole number from 4 to 20 (default 14).

regstr

Registers from a previous call (with the same p), to extend; NULL starts afresh. For dstncnt(), the registers.

a, b

Register sets to merge.

Value

dstnskch() and skchmrg() an integer vector of \(2^p\) registers; dstncnt() the estimated number of distinct values.

Details

Each value is hashed and the first p bits pick one of \(m = 2^p\) registers; the register keeps the longest run of leading zeros (plus one) seen in the remaining bits. The estimate is the bias-corrected harmonic mean \(\alpha_m m^2 / \sum_j 2^{-M_j}\) of Flajolet et al. (2007).

The estimate carries a relative standard error of about 1.04 / sqrt(2^p), so 0.8% at the default. It is an estimate: length(unique(x)) is exact when the column fits in memory. Below roughly 2.5 * 2^p distinct values the estimator switches to linear counting, which is near-exact in that range.

Values are hashed with SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) of their UTF-8 text, so the sketch is identical on every platform and across sessions. Values are compared as text (as.character()), so 1, 1.0 and "1" are one value; NA is skipped. Since a register only keeps a maximum, folding chunks with regstr and merging separate sketches with skchmrg() give the same registers as one sketch of all the data.

Errors: p not a whole number from 4 to 20; regstr not of length \(2^p\); registers that are not whole numbers from 0 to 64; two sketches of different sizes.

References

Flajolet, P., Fusy, E., Gandouet, O. and Meunier, F. (2007). HyperLogLog: the analysis of a near-optimal cardinality estimation algorithm. Analysis of Algorithms 2007, 137-156.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- sample(1:5000, 200000, replace = TRUE) # simulated
dstncnt(dstnskch(x))
#> [1] 5039.269
length(unique(x))
#> [1] 5000
dstncnt(dstnskch(c("a", "b", "c", "a", "b")))
#> [1] 3.000275
a <- dstnskch(x[1:100000])
b <- dstnskch(x[100001:200000])
dstncnt(skchmrg(a, b))
#> [1] 5039.269
try(skchmrg(dstnskch(1:10, p = 4), dstnskch(1:10, p = 5)))
#> Error : skchmrg: both sketches must have the same number of registers.
